defect.evidence_quote: We therefore hold that as a general matter determinations of reasonable suspicion and probable cause should be reviewed de novo on appeal. Having said this, we hasten to point out that a reviewing court should take care both to review findings of historical fact only for clear error and to give due weight to inferences drawn from those facts by resident judges and local law enforcement officers.
defect.problem: The holding field survives in substance, but it is truncated at '(historical…' and should state the caveat precisely: de novo review applies to ultimate reasonable-suspicion/probable-cause determinations, while historical facts get clear-error review and due weight is owed to local judge/officer inferences.
defect.proposed_fix: Ultimate determinations of reasonable suspicion for a stop and probable cause for a warrantless search are reviewed de novo on appeal; underlying historical facts are reviewed only for clear error, with due weight to reasonable inferences drawn by local judges and law-enforcement officers.

reasons: The cached opinion supports the core de novo proposition for ultimate reasonable-suspicion and probable-cause determinations.
The cached opinion also expressly limits that proposition by preserving clear-error review for historical facts and due weight for local inferences.
residual_risks: Lake has no separate holding field; support was verified from the cached opinion text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace the truncated frontmatter holding with the proposed precise formulation.
